key_insight: Boron redistributes toward defects in TiAl alloys, locally pinning dislocations and suppressing deformation twinning to increase high-temperature strength.
engineering_relevance: Controlling boron content and defect populations could help strengthen TiAl alloys, while accounting for brittle borides and interface-dependent adhesion.
method: Developed a high-fidelity machine-learning interatomic potential.
Combined hybrid grand-canonical Monte Carlo and molecular dynamics simulations.
Analyzed boron redistribution, defect interactions, and deformation mechanisms.
evidence_signal: In simulated polycrystalline TiAl at 900 K, 1 at.% boron increased average flow stress by 9.4% and reduced shear strain accumulation.
watch_item: The reported strengthening is simulation-based; experimental validation is needed to establish its transferability to processed alloys and service conditions.
paper_title: Atomistic insight into defect-mediated boron redistribution and high-temperature strengthening in TiAl alloys
